## Biological Interpretation

The differential metabolite signature strongly implicates **Glycine, serine and threonine metabolism (KEGG map00260)** as the primary affected pathway, with an extraordinary fold-enrichment of 632 and FDR near zero. Six of the nine input metabolites map to this pathway — L-threonine (C00188), pyruvic acid (C00022), oxoglutaric acid (C00026), L-glutamic acid (C00025), dihydrolipoate (C02147), and choline (C00114) — indicating a coordinated shift in one-carbon and amino-acid interconversion networks.

**L-Threonine** is a direct input to the pathway and serves as the primary driver compound; its altered abundance directly reflects disrupted flux through this network. **Dihydrolipoate** and **choline** occupy branch points linking the serine/threonine axis to methionine metabolism and one-carbon folate cycling. Pyruvic acid and oxoglutaric acid sit at the glycolytic–TCA interface; KEGG reaction-graph traversal confirms they are connected bidirectionally (pyruvate → 2-oxoglutarate via a two-hop span), consistent with bidirectional regulatory rewiring rather than a simple upstream/downstream block.

The secondary **Pyruvate metabolism (Reactome R-HSA-70268)** enriches with five compounds (C00022, C00026, C00025, C00009, C00153), consistent with niacinamide-supported NAD⁺/NADH dynamics coupling glycolysis to the observed amino-acid perturbations. **Methionine de novo and salvage pathway (Wikipathways WP3580)** ties choline and threonine metabolism together through shared methyl-donor chemistry, suggesting the treatment may impair one-carbon transfer or transsulfuration.

**Biological significance**: Coordinated elevation or depletion of these metabolites points to altered energy–amino-acid homeostasis, possibly reflecting mitochondrial stress, altered gluconeogenesis, or methylation capacity changes. The convergence of threonine, dihydrolipoate, and choline on a single hub underscores a focal disruption in one-carbon metabolism with downstream consequences for oxidative defense and biosynthetic capacity.
